<doc>
<summary>
The seed of the icon color. See <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.WaypointManager.Colors" /> for example colors.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_MeanAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above sea level, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_MeanAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above sea level, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_SurfaceAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body or sea level,
whichever is closer, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_SurfaceAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body or sea level,
whichever is closer, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_BedrockAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body, in meters.
When over water, this is the altitude above the sea floor.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_set_BedrockAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude of the waypoint above the surface of the body, in meters.
When over water, this is the altitude above the sea floor.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_NearSurface.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if the waypoint is near to the surface of a body.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Grounded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if the waypoint is attached to the ground.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Index.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The integer index of this waypoint within its cluster of sibling waypoints.
In other words, when you have a cluster of waypoints called "Somewhere Alpha",
"Somewhere Beta" and "Somewhere Gamma", the alpha site has index 0, the beta
site has index 1 and the gamma site has index 2.
When <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Waypoint.Clustered" /> is <c>false</c>, this is zero.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_Clustered.documentation:
<doc>
<summary><c>true</c> if this waypoint is part of a set of clustered waypoints with greek letter
names appended (Alpha, Beta, Gamma, etc).
If <c>true</c>, there is a one-to-one correspondence with the greek letter name and
the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Waypoint.Index" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Waypoint_get_HasContract.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the waypoint belongs to a contract.
</summary>
</doc>

WaypointManager_AddWaypoint.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Creates a waypoint at the given position at ground level, and returns a
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Waypoint" /> object that can be used to modify it.
</summary>
<param name="latitude">Latitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="longitude">Longitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="body">Celestial body the waypoint is attached to.</param>
<param name="name">Name of the waypoint.</param>
<returns></returns>
</doc>

WaypointManager_AddWaypointAtAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Creates a waypoint at the given position and altitude, and returns a
<see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Waypoint" /> object that can be used to modify it.
</summary>
<param name="latitude">Latitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="longitude">Longitude of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="altitude">Altitude (above sea level) of the waypoint.</param>
<param name="body">Celestial body the waypoint is attached to.</param>
<param name="name">Name of the waypoint.</param>
<returns></returns>
</doc>

WaypointManager_get_Waypoints.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all existing waypoints.
</summary>
</doc>

WaypointManager_get_Colors.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An example map of known color - seed pairs.
Any other integers may be used as seed.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed antennas are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy a fixed antenna.
</remarks>
</doc>

Antenna_set_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed antennas are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy a fixed antenna.
</remarks>
</doc>

Antenna_get_CanTransmit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether data can be transmitted by this antenna.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_AllowPartial.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether partial data transmission is permitted.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_set_AllowPartial.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether partial data transmission is permitted.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_Combinable.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the antenna can be combined with other antennae on the vessel
to boost the power.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_CombinableExponent.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Exponent used to calculate the combined power of multiple antennae on a vessel.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketInterval.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Interval between sending packets in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketSize.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Amount of data sent per packet in Mits.
</summary>
</doc>

Antenna_get_PacketResourceCost.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Units of electric charge consumed per packet sent.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this cargo bay.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the cargo bay.
</summary>
<remarks>
This describes where the bay's doors are, which is not the same as whether the parts
inside are sheltered: a bay whose open end has nothing attached to it never shelters
anything, however tightly shut it is. Use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Shielded" /> for that.

A cargo bay is never <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DeployableState.Broken" />, as the game
does not track damage for them.
</remarks>
</doc>

CargoBay_get_Open.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the cargo bay is open.
</summary>
</doc>

CargoBay_set_Open.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the cargo bay is open.
</summary>
</doc>

ConfigNode_HasValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns <c>true</c> if the node has a value with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the value.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns the value with the given name. If there is more than one value with
the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there is no
value with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the value.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetValues.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns all of the values with the given name, as a list.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the values.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_HasNode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns <c>true</c> if the node has a child node with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child node.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetNode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns the child node with the given name. If there is more than one child
node with the given name, the first is returned. Throws an exception if there
is no child node with the given name.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child node.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_GetNodes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns all of the child nodes with the given name, as a list.
</summary>
<param name="name">Name of the child nodes.</param>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the configuration node. For example "MODULE".
</summary>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The values stored in the node, as a dictionary mapping names to values.
</summary>
<remarks>
If a name appears more than once, only the first value is included. Use
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ConfigNode.GetValues" /> to get all of the values with a given name.
</remarks>
</doc>

ConfigNode_get_Nodes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The child nodes contained in this node.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this control surface.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_PitchEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has pitch control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_PitchEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has pitch control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_YawEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has yaw control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_YawEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has yaw control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_RollEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has roll control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_RollEnabled.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has roll control enabled.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_AuthorityLimiter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The authority limiter for the control surface, which controls how far the
control surface will move.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_AuthorityLimiter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The authority limiter for the control surface, which controls how far the
control surface will move.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Inverted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface movement is inverted.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Inverted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface movement is inverted.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has been fully deployed. Throws an exception if set
while <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, which holds the surface deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface has been fully deployed. Throws an exception if set
while <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, which holds the surface deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_DeployAngle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deploy angle of the control surface, in degrees.
</summary>
<remarks>
Applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deployed" /> is true, and clamped to the range given by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.MinDeployAngle" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.MaxDeployAngle" />. While
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> drives the
angle. A value set here takes effect when the override is released.
</remarks>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_DeployAngle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deploy angle of the control surface, in degrees.
</summary>
<remarks>
Applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deployed" /> is true, and clamped to the range given by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.MinDeployAngle" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.MaxDeployAngle" />. While
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> drives the
angle. A value set here takes effect when the override is released.
</remarks>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_MinDeployAngle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The minimum <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeployAngle" /> of the control surface, in degrees.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_MaxDeployAngle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The maximum <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeployAngle" /> of the control surface, in degrees.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_DeflectionOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs.
The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the
controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_DeflectionOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the control surface deflection is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight control. When enabled, the surface holds the deflection set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.Deflection" /> instead of responding to pitch, yaw and roll control inputs.
The prior state is restored when the override is released, when the
controlling client disconnects, or when the vessel changes.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_Deflection.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deflection command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, as a
value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface's deploy angle range.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_set_Deflection.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The deflection command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ControlSurface.DeflectionOverride" /> is enabled, as a
value between -1 and 1, mapped onto the surface's deploy angle range.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_SurfaceArea.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Surface area of the control surface in <math>m^2</math>.
</summary>
</doc>

ControlSurface_get_AvailableTorque.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available torque, in Newton meters, that can be produced by this control surface,
in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes
correspond to the coordinate axes of the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_Decouple.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Fires the decoupler. Returns the new vessel created when the decoupler fires.
Throws an exception if the decoupler has already fired.
</summary>
<remarks>
When called, the active vessel may change. It is therefore possible that,
after calling this function, the object(s) returned by previous call(s) to
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ActiveVessel" /> no longer refer to the active vessel.
</remarks>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this decoupler.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Staged.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the decoupler is enabled in the staging sequence.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_Impulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The impulse that the decoupler imparts when it is fired, in Newton seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_IsOmniDecoupler.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the decoupler is an omni-decoupler (e.g. stack separator)
</summary>
</doc>

Decoupler_get_AttachedPart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part attached to this decoupler's explosive node.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_Undock.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Undocks the docking port and returns the new <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Vessel" /> that is created.
This method can be called for either docking port in a docked pair.
Throws an exception if the docking port is not docked to anything.
</summary>
<remarks>
When called, the active vessel may change. It is therefore possible that,
after calling this function, the object(s) returned by previous call(s) to
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ActiveVessel" /> no longer refer to the active vessel.
</remarks>
</doc>

DockingPort_Position.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position of the docking port, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_Direction.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The direction that docking port points in, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The direction as a unit vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
direction is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_Rotation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rotation of the docking port, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The rotation as a quaternion of the form <math>(x, y, z, w)</math>.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
rotation is in.</param>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this docking port.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the docking port.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_DockedPart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that this docking port is docked to. Returns <c>null</c> if this
docking port is not docked to anything.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_ReengageDistance.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The distance a docking port must move away when it undocks before it
becomes ready to dock with another port, in meters.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_HasShield.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the docking port has a shield.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_Shielded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the docking ports shield, if it has one.

Returns <c>true</c> if the docking port has a shield, and the shield is
closed. Otherwise returns <c>false</c>. When set to <c>true</c>, the shield is
closed, and when set to <c>false</c> the shield is opened. If the docking
port does not have a shield, setting this attribute has no effect.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_set_Shielded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of the docking ports shield, if it has one.

Returns <c>true</c> if the docking port has a shield, and the shield is
closed. Otherwise returns <c>false</c>. When set to <c>true</c>, the shield is
closed, and when set to <c>false</c> the shield is opened. If the docking
port does not have a shield, setting this attribute has no effect.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_CanRotate.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the docking port can be commanded to rotate while docked.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_RotationLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Lock rotation. When locked, allows auto-strut to work across the joint.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_set_RotationLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Lock rotation. When locked, allows auto-strut to work across the joint.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPort_get_ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame that is fixed relative to this docking port, and
oriented with the port.
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The origin is at the position of the docking port.
</description></item><item><description>The axes rotate with the docking port.</description></item><item><description>The x-axis points out to the right side of the docking port.
</description></item><item><description>The y-axis points in the direction the docking port is facing.
</description></item><item><description>The z-axis points out of the bottom off the docking port.
</description></item></list></summary>
<remarks>
This reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the reference frame
for the part, returned by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ReferenceFrame" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_AvailableThrustAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and with its throttle set to 100%.
Returns zero if the engine does not have any fuel.
Takes the given pressure into account.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_MaxThrustAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and fueled, with its throttle and throttle limiter set to 100%.
Takes the given pressure into account.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_SpecificImpulseAt.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The specific impulse of the engine under the given pressure, in seconds. Returns zero
if the engine is not active.
</summary>
<param name="pressure">Atmospheric pressure in atmospheres</param>
</doc>

Engine_ToggleThrustReversal.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Toggle the engine's thrust reverser. Throws an exception if the engine
does not have a thrust reverser (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanReverseThrust" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine is active. Setting this attribute may have no effect,
depending on <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanShutdown" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanRestart" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine is active. Setting this attribute may have no effect,
depending on <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanShutdown" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanRestart" />.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Thrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current amount of thrust being produced by the engine, in Newtons.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_AvailableThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and with its throttle set to 100%.
Returns zero if the engine does not have any fuel.
Takes the engine's current <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.ThrustLimit" /> and atmospheric conditions
into account.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_MaxThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the engine
when activated and fueled, with its throttle and throttle limiter set to 100%.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_MaxVacuumThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The maximum amount of thrust that can be produced by the engine in a
vacuum, in Newtons. This is the amount of thrust produced by the engine
when activated, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.ThrustLimit" /> is set to 100%, the main
vessel's throttle is set to 100% and the engine is in a vacuum.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_ThrustLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The thrust limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1. Setting this
attribute may have no effect, for example the thrust limit for a solid
rocket booster cannot be changed in flight.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_ThrustLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The thrust limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1. Setting this
attribute may have no effect, for example the thrust limit for a solid
rocket booster cannot be changed in flight.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Thrusters.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The components of the engine that generate thrust.
</summary>
<remarks>
For example, this corresponds to the rocket nozzel on a solid rocket booster,
or the individual nozzels on a RAPIER engine.
The overall thrust produced by the engine, as reported by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.AvailableThrust" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.MaxThrust" /> and others, is the sum of the thrust generated by each thruster.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_get_SpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current specific impulse of the engine, in seconds. Returns zero
if the engine is not active.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_VacuumSpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The vacuum specific impulse of the engine, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_KerbinSeaLevelSpecificImpulse.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The specific impulse of the engine at sea level on Kerbin, in seconds.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantNames.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The names of the propellants that the engine consumes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Propellants.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The propellants that the engine consumes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantRatios.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The ratio of resources that the engine consumes. A dictionary mapping resource names
to the ratio at which they are consumed by the engine.
</summary>
<remarks>
For example, if the ratios are 0.6 for LiquidFuel and 0.4 for Oxidizer, then for every
0.6 units of LiquidFuel that the engine burns, it will burn 0.4 units of Oxidizer.
</remarks>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasFuel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has any fuel available.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Flameout.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has flamed out - it is active but has run out of
propellant, so it is producing no thrust. This is the signal a client
can use to decide when to activate the next stage. Note that on a
vessel with drop tanks or asparagus staging some engines can flame out
while others keep burning.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Throttle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current throttle setting for the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
This is not necessarily the same as the vessel's main throttle
setting, as some engines take time to adjust their throttle
(such as jet engines), or independent throttle may be enabled.

When the engine's independent throttle is enabled
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.IndependentThrottle" />), can be used to set the throttle percentage.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_Throttle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current throttle setting for the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
This is not necessarily the same as the vessel's main throttle
setting, as some engines take time to adjust their throttle
(such as jet engines), or independent throttle may be enabled.

When the engine's independent throttle is enabled
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.IndependentThrottle" />), can be used to set the throttle percentage.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_ThrottleLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Throttle" /> affects the engine. For example,
this is <c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets, and <c>false</c> for solid rocket
boosters.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_IndependentThrottle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the independent throttle is enabled for the engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_IndependentThrottle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the independent throttle is enabled for the engine.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_CanRestart.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine can be restarted once shutdown. If the engine cannot be shutdown,
returns <c>false</c>. For example, this is <c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets
and <c>false</c> for solid rocket boosters.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_CanShutdown.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine can be shutdown once activated. For example, this is
<c>true</c> for liquid fueled rockets and <c>false</c> for solid rocket boosters.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasModes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has multiple modes of operation.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Mode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the current engine mode.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_Mode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the current engine mode.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_Modes.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available modes for the engine.
A dictionary mapping mode names to <see cref="T:SpaceCenter.Engine" /> objects.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_AutoModeSwitch.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine will automatically switch modes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_AutoModeSwitch.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine will automatically switch modes.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_GimbalRange.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The range over which the gimbal can move, in degrees.
Returns 0 if the engine is not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_GimbalLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engines gimbal is locked in place. Setting this attribute has
no effect if the engine is not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_GimbalLocked.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engines gimbal is locked in place. Setting this attribute has
no effect if the engine is not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_GimbalLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The gimbal limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
Returns 0 if the gimbal is locked.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_GimbalLimit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The gimbal limiter of the engine. A value between 0 and 1.
Returns 0 if the gimbal is locked.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_GimbalOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the gimbal is being controlled directly, bypassing the vessel's normal
flight controls. When enabled, the gimbal deflection is set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalActuation" /> instead of the normal control inputs.
The override is automatically released if the controlling client disconnects or the
vessel changes. Has no effect if the engine is not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_GimbalOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the gimbal is being controlled directly, bypassing the vessel's normal
flight controls. When enabled, the gimbal deflection is set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalActuation" /> instead of the normal control inputs.
The override is automatically released if the controlling client disconnects or the
vessel changes. Has no effect if the engine is not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_GimbalActuation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The gimbal actuation command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalOverride" /> is enabled, in
the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1
and 1. The physical deflection is scaled by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalRange" />
and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalLimit" />. When the gimbal is not being overridden,
returns the current actuation.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_GimbalActuation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The gimbal actuation command applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalOverride" /> is enabled, in
the pitch, roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1
and 1. The physical deflection is scaled by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalRange" />
and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.GimbalLimit" />. When the gimbal is not being overridden,
returns the current actuation.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_AvailableTorque.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available torque, in Newton meters, that can be produced by this engine,
in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes
correspond to the coordinate axes of the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />.
Returns zero if the engine is inactive, or not gimballed.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_CanReverseThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine has a recognized thrust reverser. This is <c>true</c> for
stock engines with a thrust reverser (such as the J-33 "Wheesley" and
J-90 "Goliath" turbofan engines) and for selected mod engines. It is
<c>false</c> for engines whose reverser is not recognized, as KSP provides no
standard way to detect one.
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_ThrustReversed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine's thrust reverser is engaged, reversing the
direction of thrust. While the reverser is still moving, this reports
the state it is moving to, so a read immediately after a set returns
the value that was set and setting the same value again has no effect.
Throws an exception if the engine does not have a thrust reverser
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanReverseThrust" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_set_ThrustReversed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine's thrust reverser is engaged, reversing the
direction of thrust. While the reverser is still moving, this reports
the state it is moving to, so a read immediately after a set returns
the value that was set and setting the same value again has no effect.
Throws an exception if the engine does not have a thrust reverser
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.CanReverseThrust" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasRealFuels.documentation: Whether the engine is managed by RealFuels. The remaining properties in this section are only available when it is.

Engine_get_Ignitions.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The number of times the engine can still be ignited, or -1 if it can be ignited an
unlimited number of times. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by
RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_IgnitionResources.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The resources the engine consumes each time it ignites, keyed by resource name, with
the amount of each that is required. The engine uses up an ignition and fails to
light if they are not available. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by
RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasUllage.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine's propellant is subject to ullage, so that it must be settled
before the engine will run reliably. Throws an exception if the engine is not
managed by RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantStability.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
How settled the propellant feeding the engine is, from 0 (fully unsettled) to 1
(fully settled). Acceleration along the engine's thrust axis settles it, and
coasting and rotation unsettle it. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed
by RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PropellantReliability.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The probability that the propellant feeding the engine behaves normally, from 0 to 1.
This is <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.PropellantStability" /> scaled by the game's ullage difficulty
setting, and is the value RealFuels itself tests against when deciding whether the
engine runs. Throws an exception if the engine is not managed by RealFuels
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_PressureFed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the engine is fed by tank pressure rather than by a pump, and so needs to
draw from a highly pressurized tank. Throws an exception if the engine is not
managed by RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Engine_get_HasFeedPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the tanks feeding the engine supply the pressure it needs. Always
<c>true</c> for an engine that is not pressure fed. Throws an exception if the
engine is not managed by RealFuels (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.HasRealFuels" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_Transmit.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Transmit all experimental data contained by this part.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_Dump.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Dump the experimental data contained by the experiment.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this experiment.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Name.documentation: Internal name of the experiment, as used in part cfg files.

Experiment_get_Title.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Title of the experiment, as shown on the in-game UI.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the experiment has been deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Rerunnable.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the experiment can be re-run.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Data.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The data contained in this experiment.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Available.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Determines if the experiment is available given the current conditions.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_Biome.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the biome the experiment is currently in.
</summary>
</doc>

Experiment_get_ScienceSubject.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Containing information on the corresponding specific science result for the current
conditions. Returns <c>null</c> if the experiment is unavailable.
</summary>
</doc>

Fairing_Jettison.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Jettison the fairing. Has no effect if it has already been jettisoned.
</summary>
</doc>

Fairing_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this fairing.
</summary>
</doc>

Fairing_get_Jettisoned.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the fairing has been jettisoned.
</summary>
</doc>

Force_Remove.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Remove the force.
</summary>
<remarks>
Any further use of this object throws an exception.
</remarks>
</doc>

Force_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that this force is applied to.
</summary>
</doc>

Force_get_ForceVector.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The force vector, in Newtons.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts,
with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.</returns>
</doc>

Force_set_ForceVector.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The force vector, in Newtons.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts,
with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.</returns>
</doc>

Force_get_Position.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position at which the force acts, in reference frame <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Force.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
</doc>

Force_set_Position.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position at which the force acts, in reference frame <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Force.ReferenceFrame" />.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
</doc>

Force_get_ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame of the force vector and position.
</summary>
</doc>

Force_set_ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame of the force vector and position.
</summary>
</doc>

Intake_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this intake.
</summary>
</doc>

Intake_get_Speed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Speed of the flow into the intake, in <math>m/s</math>.
</summary>
</doc>

Intake_get_Flow.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate of flow into the intake, in units of resource per second.
</summary>
</doc>

Intake_get_Area.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The area of the intake's opening, in square meters.
</summary>
</doc>

LaunchClamp_Release.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Releases the docking clamp. Has no effect if the clamp has already been released.
</summary>
</doc>

LaunchClamp_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this launch clamp.
</summary>
</doc>

Leg_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this landing leg.
</summary>
</doc>

Leg_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the landing leg.
</summary>
</doc>

Leg_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the landing leg is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed landing legs are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy fixed landing gear.
</remarks>
</doc>

Leg_set_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the landing leg is deployed.
</summary>
<remarks>
Fixed landing legs are always deployed.
Returns an error if you try to deploy fixed landing gear.
</remarks>
</doc>

Leg_get_IsGrounded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Returns whether the leg is touching the ground.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this light.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_get_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the light is switched on.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_set_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the light is switched on.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_get_BlinkRate.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The blink rate of the light.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_set_BlinkRate.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The blink rate of the light.
</summary>
</doc>

Light_get_PowerUsage.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current power usage, in units of charge per second.
</summary>
</doc>

Module_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Name of the PartModule. For example, "ModuleEngines".
</summary>
</doc>

Module_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that contains this module.
</summary>
</doc>

Module_get_Config.documentation: The static configuration of the module, as found in the part's cfg file. This provides access to data that is not exposed as a field, such as the resources produced by a generator. Returns null if the module's configuration node cannot be found.

Module_get_FieldList.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all the fields of the module, including those not visible in the right-click
menu of the part. Filter by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Visible" /> to get just the visible ones.
</summary>
</doc>

Module_get_EventList.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all the events of the module, including those not currently visible or active.
Events are the clickable buttons visible in the right-click menu of the part. Filter by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartEvent.Visible" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartEvent.Active" /> to get just the ones
shown in the menu.
</summary>
</doc>

Module_get_ActionList.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all the actions of the module. These are the parts actions that can be assigned
to action groups in the in-game editor.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_Deploy.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Deploys the parachute. This has no effect if the parachute has already
been deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_Arm.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Deploys the parachute. This has no effect if the parachute has already
been armed or deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_Part.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part object for this parachute.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_Deployed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the parachute has been deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_Armed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the parachute has been armed or deployed.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_State.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current state of the parachute.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_DeployAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude at which the parachute will full deploy, in meters.
Only applicable to stock parachutes.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_set_DeployAltitude.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The altitude at which the parachute will full deploy, in meters.
Only applicable to stock parachutes.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_DeployMinPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The minimum pressure at which the parachute will semi-deploy, in atmospheres.
Only applicable to stock parachutes.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_set_DeployMinPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The minimum pressure at which the parachute will semi-deploy, in atmospheres.
Only applicable to stock parachutes.
</summary>
</doc>

Parachute_get_SafeState.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether it is currently safe to deploy the parachute, given the vessel's
flight conditions. Computed by KSP from the current airspeed, pressure and
temperature. Only applicable to stock parachutes.
Note that KSP reports <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ParachuteSafeState.Unsafe" /> for the first
second after the vessel unpacks, before its thermal data is valid.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_BuoyantForceAt.documentation: The buoyant force on the part when fully submerged in a fluid of the given density, in Newtons. The density of the fluid, in kg/m^3. The acceleration due to gravity, in m/s^2. Applies and , so the result is what the game would do to the part rather than what Archimedes' principle alone gives.

Part_Position.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position of the part in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
<remarks>
This is a fixed position in the part, defined by the parts model.
It s not necessarily the same as the parts center of mass.
Use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfMass" /> to get the parts center of mass.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_CenterOfMass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The position of the parts center of mass in the given reference frame.
If the part is physicsless in flight, this is equivalent to <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Position" />.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
</doc>

Part_BoundingBox.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The axis-aligned bounding box of the part in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The positions of the minimum and maximum vertices of the box.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vectors are in.</param>
<remarks>
This is computed from the meshes that make up the parts model, and covers only
this part - the models of any child parts are excluded.
If the part has no visible model, the box has zero volume and is centered on
the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfMass" /> of the part.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_Direction.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The direction the part points in, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The direction as a unit vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
direction is in.</param>
</doc>

Part_Velocity.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The linear velocity of the part in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The velocity as a vector. The vector points in the direction of travel,
and its magnitude is the speed of the body in meters per second.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
velocity vector is in.</param>
</doc>

Part_Rotation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rotation of the part, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The rotation as a quaternion of the form <math>(x, y, z, w)</math>.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
rotation is in.</param>
</doc>

Part_Lift.documentation: The aerodynamic lift currently acting on the part. A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons. The reference frame that the returned vector is in. Not available when the Ferram Aerospace Research mod is installed.

Part_Drag.documentation: The aerodynamic drag currently acting on the part. A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts, with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons. The reference frame that the returned vector is in. Not available when the Ferram Aerospace Research mod is installed.

Part_CenterOfBuoyancy.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The point the buoyant force on the part acts at, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
<remarks>
A submerged part reports the point the game applied the force at, which it shifts
towards the submerged part of the hull. Any other part reports its configured
center of buoyancy.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_CenterOfDisplacement.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The point the depth of the part is measured at, in the given reference frame.
</summary>
<returns>The position as a vector.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
position vector is in.</param>
</doc>

Part_BuoyantForce.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The buoyant force currently acting on the part.
</summary>
<returns>A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts,
with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.</returns>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the returned
vector is in.</param>
<remarks>
The buoyant force on its own. The water drag and lift the game applies alongside
it are reported by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.SubmergedDragMultiplier" /> and
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.SubmergedLiftMultiplier" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_AddForce.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Exert a constant force on the part, acting at the given position.
</summary>
<returns>An object that can be used to remove or modify the force.</returns>
<param name="force">A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts,
with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.</param>
<param name="position">The position at which the force acts, as a vector.</param>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the
force and position are in.</param>
<remarks>
The force is removed when the client that added it disconnects.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_InstantaneousForce.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Exert an instantaneous force on the part, acting at the given position.
</summary>
<param name="force">A vector pointing in the direction that the force acts,
with its magnitude equal to the strength of the force in Newtons.</param>
<param name="position">The position at which the force acts, as a vector.</param>
<param name="referenceFrame">The reference frame that the
force and position are in.</param>
<remarks>The force is applied instantaneously in a single physics update.</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_Name.documentation: Internal name of the part, as used in part cfg files. For example "Mark1-2Pod".

Part_get_Title.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Title of the part, as shown when the part is right clicked in-game. For example "Mk1-2 Command Pod".
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Config.documentation: The static configuration of the part, as found in its part cfg file. This provides access to data that is not exposed elsewhere, such as the configuration of the part's modules. Returns null if the part has no associated configuration node.

Part_get_Tag.documentation: The name tag for the part. Can be set to a custom string using the in-game user interface. Throws an exception if no name tag part module is installed. The name tag part module is provided by KSPCommunityPartModules 0.5 or later, or by kOS, which shares this string.

Part_set_Tag.documentation: The name tag for the part. Can be set to a custom string using the in-game user interface. Throws an exception if no name tag part module is installed. The name tag part module is provided by KSPCommunityPartModules 0.5 or later, or by kOS, which shares this string.

Part_get_FlagURL.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The asset URL for the part's flag.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_set_FlagURL.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The asset URL for the part's flag.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Highlighted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is highlighted.
</summary>
<remarks>
The highlighting is removed when the client that enabled it disconnects.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_set_Highlighted.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is highlighted.
</summary>
<remarks>
The highlighting is removed when the client that enabled it disconnects.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_HighlightColor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The color used to highlight the part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_set_HighlightColor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The color used to highlight the part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Cost.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The cost of the part, in units of funds.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Vessel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The vessel that contains this part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Parent.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The parts parent. Returns <c>null</c> if the part does not have a parent.
This, in combination with <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Children" />, can be used to traverse the vessels
parts tree.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Children.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The parts children. Returns an empty list if the part has no children.
This, in combination with <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Parent" />, can be used to traverse the vessels
parts tree.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_AxiallyAttached.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is axially attached to its parent, i.e. on the top
or bottom of its parent. If the part has no parent, returns <c>false</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RadiallyAttached.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is radially attached to its parent, i.e. on the side of its parent.
If the part has no parent, returns <c>false</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Stage.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The stage in which this part will be activated. Returns -1 if the part is not
activated by staging.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_DecoupleStage.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The stage in which this part will be decoupled. Returns -1 if the part is never
decoupled from the vessel.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Mass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The current mass of the part, including resources it contains, in kilograms.
Returns zero if the part is massless.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_DryMass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The mass of the part, not including any resources it contains, in kilograms.
Returns zero if the part is massless.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Shielded.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is shielded from the exterior of the vessel, for example by a fairing.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_DynamicPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The dynamic pressure acting on the part, in Pascals.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_StaticPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The static pressure acting on the part, in Pascals. Below the waterline this
includes the pressure of the water.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Displacement.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The volume of water the part displaces when fully submerged, in <math>m^3</math>.
</summary>
<remarks>
See <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.DisplacedVolume" /> for the volume it is displacing now.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_BuoyancyMultiplier.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The multiplier applied to the buoyant force on the part. One for most parts.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Splashed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the part is in contact with water.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_SubmergedPortion.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The fraction of the part below the waterline, between 0 and 1.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_DisplacedVolume.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The volume of water the part is displacing, in <math>m^3</math>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Depth.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The depth of the part below the waterline, in meters, measured at
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfDisplacement" />. Negative above the waterline. Returns zero
if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MinDepth.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The depth of the shallowest point of the part below the waterline, in meters.
Returns zero if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MaxDepth.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The depth of the deepest point of the part below the waterline, in meters.
Returns zero if the body the vessel is at has no ocean.
</summary>
<remarks>
The game ramps the buoyant force in over the first fraction of a meter of this
depth.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_SubmergedDynamicPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The dynamic pressure of the water acting on the part, in Pascals.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_SubmergedDragMultiplier.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The multiplier applied to the drag on the part while it is submerged.
</summary>
<remarks>
The game sets this high on splashdown and eases it down as the part moves through
the water. It climbs back once the part slows to a crawl, so a hull under way
reads lower than one lying still.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_SubmergedLiftMultiplier.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The multiplier applied to the lift on the part while it is submerged.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_WaterAngularDragMultiplier.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The multiplier applied to the angular drag on the part while it is submerged.
</summary>
<remarks>
Part of the part's configuration rather than a live readout, so it reads the same
in the editor and at a body with no ocean.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_ImpactTolerance.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The impact tolerance of the part, in meters per second.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Temperature.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Temperature of the part, in Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_SkinTemperature.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Temperature of the skin of the part, in Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MaxTemperature.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Maximum temperature that the part can survive, in Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MaxSkinTemperature.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Maximum temperature that the skin of the part can survive, in Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MaxPressure.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Maximum pressure that the part can survive, in Pascals.
</summary>
<remarks>
With part pressure limits enabled in the difficulty settings, the part is destroyed
when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.StaticPressure" /> plus <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.DynamicPressure" /> exceeds this.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalMass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A measure of how much energy it takes to increase the internal temperature of the part,
in Joules per Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalSkinMass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A measure of how much energy it takes to increase the skin temperature of the part,
in Joules per Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalResourceMass.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A measure of how much energy it takes to increase the temperature of the resources
contained in the part, in Joules per Kelvin.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalInternalFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is begin generated by the part.
For example, some engines generate heat by combusting fuel.
Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is losing
heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalConductionFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is conducting into or out of the part via contact with
other parts. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalConvectionFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is convecting into or out of the part from the
surrounding atmosphere. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalRadiationFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is radiating into or out of the part from the surrounding
environment. Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part is gaining heat energy, and negative means it is
losing heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ThermalSkinToInternalFlux.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which heat energy is transferring between the part's skin and its internals.
Measured in energy per unit time, or power, in Watts.
A positive value means the part's internals are gaining heat energy,
and negative means its skin is gaining heat energy.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Resources.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Resources" /> object for the part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_CrewCapacity.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The number of crew members that can occupy the part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Crew.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The crew members occupying the part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_AvailableSeats.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
How many open seats the part has.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Crossfeed.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether this part is crossfeed capable.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_IsFuelLine.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether this part is a fuel line.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_FuelLinesFrom.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The parts that are connected to this part via fuel lines, where the direction of the
fuel line is into this part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_FuelLinesTo.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The parts that are connected to this part via fuel lines, where the direction of the
fuel line is out of this part.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Antenna.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Antenna" /> if the part is an antenna, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
<remarks>
If RemoteTech is installed, this will always return <c>null</c>.
To interact with RemoteTech antennas, use the RemoteTech service APIs.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_CargoBay.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CargoBay" /> if the part is a cargo bay, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ControlSurface.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ControlSurface" /> if the part is an aerodynamic control surface,
otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Decoupler.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Decoupler" /> if the part is a decoupler, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_DockingPort.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.DockingPort" /> if the part is a docking port, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ResourceDrain.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ResourceDrain" /> if the part is a resource drain, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Engine.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Engine" /> if the part is an engine, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Experiment.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Experiment" /> if the part contains a
single science experiment, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
<remarks>
Throws an exception if the part contains more than one experiment.
In that case, use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Experiments" /> to get the list of experiments in the part.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_Experiments.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Experiment" /> objects that the part contains.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Fairing.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Fairing" /> if the part is a fairing, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Intake.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
An <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Intake" /> if the part is an intake, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
<remarks>
This includes any part that generates thrust. This covers many different types
of engine, including liquid fuel rockets, solid rocket boosters and jet engines.
For RCS thrusters see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RCS" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_Leg.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Leg" /> if the part is a landing leg, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_LaunchClamp.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.LaunchClamp" /> if the part is a launch clamp, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Light.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Light" /> if the part is a light, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Parachute.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Parachute" /> if the part is a parachute, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Radiator.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Radiator" /> if the part is a radiator, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RCS.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RCS" /> if the part is an RCS block/thruster, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ReactionWheel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ReactionWheel" /> if the part is a reaction wheel, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ResourceConverter.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ResourceConverter" /> if the part is a resource converter,
otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ResourceHarvester.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.ResourceHarvester" /> if the part is a resource harvester,
otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Sensor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Sensor" /> if the part is a sensor, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_SolarPanel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.SolarPanel" /> if the part is a solar panel, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_Wheel.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Wheel" /> if the part is a wheel, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RoboticController.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RoboticController" /> if the part is a robotic controller,
otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RoboticHinge.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RoboticHinge" /> if the part is a robotic hinge, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RoboticPiston.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RoboticPiston" /> if the part is a robotic piston, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RoboticRotation.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RoboticRotation" /> if the part is a robotic rotation servo, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_RoboticRotor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.RoboticRotor" /> if the part is a robotic rotor, otherwise <c>null</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_MomentOfInertia.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The moment of inertia of the part in <math>kg.m^2</math> around its center of mass
in the parts center of mass reference frame (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfMassReferenceFrame" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_InertiaTensor.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The inertia tensor of the part around its center of mass, in the parts center of
mass reference frame (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfMassReferenceFrame" />).
Returns the 3x3 matrix as a list of elements, in row-major order.
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_ReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame that is fixed relative to this part, and centered on a fixed
position within the part, defined by the parts model.
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The origin is at the position of the part, as returned by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Position" />.</description></item><item><description>The axes rotate with the part.</description></item><item><description>The x, y and z axis directions depend on the design of the part.
</description></item></list></summary>
<remarks>
For docking port parts, this reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the
reference frame for the docking port, returned by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DockingPort.ReferenceFrame" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_CenterOfMassReferenceFrame.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The reference frame that is fixed relative to this part, and centered on its
center of mass.
<list type="bullet"><item><description>The origin is at the center of mass of the part, as returned by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.CenterOfMass" />.</description></item><item><description>The axes rotate with the part.</description></item><item><description>The x, y and z axis directions depend on the design of the part.
</description></item></list></summary>
<remarks>
For docking port parts, this reference frame is not necessarily equivalent to the
reference frame for the docking port, returned by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DockingPort.ReferenceFrame" />.
</remarks>
</doc>

Part_get_HasRealFuelsTank.documentation: Whether the part is a fuel tank managed by RealFuels. The remaining properties in this section are only available when it is.

Part_get_HighlyPressurized.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the tank is highly pressurized, which is what a pressure-fed engine needs to
draw from (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Engine.PressureFed" />). Throws an exception if the part is
not a RealFuels fuel tank (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.HasRealFuelsTank" />).
</summary>
</doc>

Part_get_BoiloffRate.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rate at which the tank's cryogenic contents are boiling off, in kilograms per
second of in-game time, measured over the last update RealFuels computed it in.
The contents keep boiling off under time warp, where that update covers a much
longer span of in-game time than a physics frame does. The rate is zero for a
tank holding nothing cryogenic, for one still being fed by a launch clamp, whose
temperature RealFuels holds down instead, and in the editor. Throws an exception
if the part is not a RealFuels fuel tank (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.HasRealFuelsTank" />).
</summary>
</doc>

PartAction_get_Module.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module that contains this action.
</summary>
</doc>

PartAction_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The identifier of the action. This is stable and does not change between game versions,
unlike <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartAction.GuiName" />.
</summary>
</doc>

PartAction_get_GuiName.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the action, as displayed in the in-game editor.
</summary>
</doc>

PartAction_set_Activated.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Activate or deactivate the action. Equivalent to triggering the action from an action
group. Set to <c>true</c> to activate the action, or <c>false</c> to deactivate it.
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_Trigger.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Trigger the event. Equivalent to clicking the button in the right-click menu of the part.
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_get_Module.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module that contains this event.
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The identifier of the event. This is stable and does not change between game versions,
unlike <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartEvent.GuiName" />.
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_get_GuiName.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the event, as displayed in the right-click menu of the part.
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_get_Visible.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the event is visible in the right-click menu of the part, in the current scene
(flight or editor).
</summary>
</doc>

PartEvent_get_Active.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the event is currently active.
</summary>
</doc>

PartField_Reset.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Set the value of the field to its original value.
</summary>
<remarks>
The original value is the value the field had when the part was loaded.
Works for any field, including those not visible in the right-click menu.
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_get_Module.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module that contains this field.
</summary>
</doc>

PartField_get_Name.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The identifier of the field. This is stable and does not change between game versions,
unlike <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.GuiName" />.
</summary>
</doc>

PartField_get_GuiName.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the field, as displayed in the right-click menu of the part. This may be
empty for fields that are not visible in the menu.
</summary>
</doc>

PartField_get_Visible.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the field is visible in the right-click menu of the part, in the current scene
(flight or editor).
</summary>
</doc>

PartField_get_Value.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of the field, as a string. This works for fields of any type, and returns the
same string that is shown in the right-click menu of the part.
</summary>
<remarks>
Setting the value using this property is only permitted for string fields. Use the typed
properties (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.BoolValue" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.IntValue" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.FloatValue" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.DoubleValue" />) to set fields of other types.
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_set_Value.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of the field, as a string. This works for fields of any type, and returns the
same string that is shown in the right-click menu of the part.
</summary>
<remarks>
Setting the value using this property is only permitted for string fields. Use the typed
properties (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.BoolValue" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.IntValue" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.FloatValue" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.DoubleValue" />) to set fields of other types.
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_get_BoolValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a boolean field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a boolean field
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_set_BoolValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a boolean field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a boolean field
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_get_IntValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of an integer field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not an integer field
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_set_IntValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of an integer field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not an integer field
(see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_get_FloatValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a single precision floating point field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a single precision floating point
field (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_set_FloatValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a single precision floating point field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a single precision floating point
field (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_get_DoubleValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a double precision floating point field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a double precision floating point
field (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

PartField_set_DoubleValue.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The value of a double precision floating point field.
</summary>
<remarks>
The getter throws an exception if the field is not a double precision floating point
field (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.PartField.Type" />).
</remarks>
</doc>

Parts_WithName.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of parts whose <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Name" /> is <paramref name="name" />.
</summary>
<param name="name"></param>
</doc>

Parts_WithTitle.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A list of all parts whose <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Part.Title" /> is <paramref name="title" />.
</summary>
<param name="title"></param>
</doc>

Parts_WithTag.documentation:

Parts_get_Controlling.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part from which the vessel is controlled.
Returns <c>null</c> if the vessel has no control point, in which case it is
oriented by its root part.
</summary>
<remarks>
A vessel gets no control point when it is created by a decoupler or an undocking
and none of its parts is a command module with crew aboard. A probe core does not
give it one either. Assign this property to choose the control point, which is
equivalent to "Control From Here" in game.
</remarks>
</doc>

RCS_OverrideWrench.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The force and torque the given demands would produce, in Newtons and Newton meters.
</summary>
<returns>The force, and the torque about the vessel's center of mass, in the vessel's
reference frame (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />), or zero if the RCS is
inactive.</returns>
<param name="rotation">A rotation demand, as set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.RotationOverride" />.</param>
<param name="translation">A translation demand, as set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.TranslationOverride" />.</param>
<remarks>
The demands do not have to be applied. The prediction leaves out full thrust, which
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.Force" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.Torque" /> include.
</remarks>
</doc>
