RCS_get_InputOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the RCS control is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight controls. When enabled, the rotation and translation demand is set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.RotationOverride" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.TranslationOverride" /> instead of the
normal control inputs. The override is automatically released if the
controlling client disconnects or the vessel changes.
Precision mode leaves an overridden block at full thrust.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_set_InputOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the RCS control is being set directly, bypassing the vessel's
normal flight controls. When enabled, the rotation and translation demand is set by
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.RotationOverride" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.TranslationOverride" /> instead of the
normal control inputs. The override is automatically released if the
controlling client disconnects or the vessel changes.
Precision mode leaves an overridden block at full thrust.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_RotationOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rotation demand applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is enabled, in the pitch,
roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_set_RotationOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The rotation demand applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is enabled, in the pitch,
roll and yaw axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1 and 1.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_TranslationOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The translation demand applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is enabled, in the
right, up and forward axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1
and 1.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_set_TranslationOverride.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The translation demand applied when <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is enabled, in the
right, up and forward axes. Each component is a normalized control input between -1
and 1.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_AvailableTorque.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available torque, in Newton meters, that can be produced by this RCS,
in the positive and negative pitch, roll and yaw axes of the vessel. These axes
correspond to the coordinate axes of the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />.
Returns zero if RCS is disable.
</summary>
<remarks>
Precision mode weakens the block, and the available torque follows it. A block
driven by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is exempt, so <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.OverrideWrench" />
can report the larger torque an override reaches.
</remarks>
</doc>

RCS_get_AvailableForce.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The available force, in Newtons, that can be produced by this RCS,
in the positive and negative x, y and z axes of the vessel. These axes
correspond to the coordinate axes of the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />.
Returns zero if RCS is disabled.
</summary>
<remarks>
Precision mode weakens the block, and the available force follows it. A block
driven by <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.InputOverride" /> is exempt, so <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.OverrideWrench" />
can report the larger force an override reaches.
</remarks>
</doc>

RCS_get_Force.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The force being applied by the RCS thrusters, in Newtons. The vector is in the
vessel's reference frame (<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />).
Returns zero if the RCS is inactive.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_Torque.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The torque being applied by the RCS thrusters about the vessel's center of mass,
in Newton meters. The vector is in the vessel's reference frame
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.ReferenceFrame" />). Returns zero if the RCS is inactive.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_AvailableThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The amount of thrust, in Newtons, that would be produced by the thruster when activated.
Returns zero if the thruster does not have any fuel.
Takes the thrusters current <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.ThrustLimit" /> and atmospheric conditions
into account.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_MaxThrust.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The maximum amount of thrust that can be produced by the RCS thrusters when active,
in Newtons, with the <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.RCS.ThrustLimit" /> set to 100%.
Takes atmospheric conditions into account.
</summary>
</doc>

RCS_get_MaxVacuumThrust.documentation:

</summary>
</doc>

ClosestApproach.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
A close approach between an orbit and a target orbit. Obtained by calling
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.NextClosestApproach" /> or <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Orbit.ClosestApproaches" />.
</summary>
<remarks>
The object names the approach rather than describing it once: each member
estimates the time of closest approach from where the two orbits are now, and
describes the state at that time. The estimate moves as the game runs, so
members read at different moments can differ a little; members read in one
physics tick all describe the same estimate. Relative quantities are the target
relative to the orbiting object (target minus self).

The search runs forward over one orbital period from the current time. Once an
approach has passed and the two orbits are moving apart, the closest point in
that period is the current one, so the object reports the approach as now, at
the present separation, until the orbits bring another one within range.
</remarks>
</doc>

Control.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Used to manipulate the controls of a vessel. This includes adjusting the
throttle, enabling/disabling systems such as SAS and RCS, or altering the
direction in which the vessel is pointing.
Obtained by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Vessel.Control" />.
</summary>
<remarks>
Control inputs (pitch, yaw, roll, translation, wheel throttle, wheel steering
and the custom axes) are zeroed when all clients that have set one or more of
these inputs are no longer connected. The throttle is an exception: it keeps
its value when clients disconnect.

A kerbal on EVA is a vessel, and is driven by these same controls. The
translation inputs move it: <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Forward" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Right" /> walk
it about, relative to the direction it is facing, and all three translate its
jetpack once that is deployed. Walking is not throttled by the size of the
input, only started by it. The rotation inputs turn it, at a rate proportional
to the input: <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Yaw" /> steers it as it walks, and all three turn its
jetpack. Turning the jetpack releases the kerbal from the orientation it was
holding; it stops and holds its new orientation once the input returns to zero.
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.RCS" /> deploys and stows the jetpack and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Lights" />
switches the helmet lamp. The remaining controls do nothing for a kerbal.
A kerbal is also sent out and brought back in from here: with
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.CrewMember.EVA" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.Board" />, and
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.GrabLadder" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.ReleaseLadder" /> for the ladders it
passes on the way.
</remarks>
</doc>

MitigationMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls one of the auto-pilot's individually-toggleable oscillation mitigations
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationBandwidthFloorMode" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationFeedforwardMode" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.OscillationOutputFilterMode" />).
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Automatic
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The default: the mitigation engages automatically, driven by the runtime oscillation
detector and the hold gate. Rigid vessels are left untouched.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Off
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The mitigation never engages. The other mitigations are unaffected.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Forced
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The mitigation is fully engaged at all times, regardless of what the oscillation
detector reports.
</summary>
</doc>

RateFilterMode.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Controls the auto-pilot's rate-feedback filtering for an axis group, the mitigation that
removes a structural oscillation (wobble) from the measured angular velocity before the
control loops consume it.
See <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchYawRateFilterMode" /> and <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.RollRateFilterMode" />.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Automatic
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The default. The auto-pilot detects structural oscillation at runtime, estimates its
frequency and routes it to the appropriate filter: a notch for a low-frequency mode
near the control band, a low-pass for a high-frequency mode, or a broadband low-pass
while the frequency is not yet known. Rigid vessels are left untouched.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Off
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
No rate filtering. The other oscillation mitigations are unaffected.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Notch
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Force a notch filter at the manually set frequency
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.PitchYawOscillationFrequency" /> /
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.AutoPilot.RollOscillationFrequency" />), for a vessel whose structural mode
is known in advance.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: LowPass
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Force a low-pass filter derived from the manually set frequency.
</summary>
</doc>

DeployableState.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of a deployable part.
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Antenna.State" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.CargoBay.State" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Leg.State" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Radiator.State" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ResourceHarvester.State" />, <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.SolarPanel.State" />,
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Wheel.State" /></summary>
</doc>

values.name: Deployed
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part is fully deployed. A cargo bay in this state is fully open.
Parts that cannot be retracted, such as fixed radiators, solar panels,
antennas, landing legs and wheels, are always in this state.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Retracted
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part is fully retracted. A cargo bay in this state is closed and locked.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Deploying
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part is being deployed. A cargo bay in this state is opening.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Retracting
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part is being retracted. A cargo bay in this state is closing.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Broken
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part is broken. Cargo bays and resource harvesters never report
this state, as the game does not track damage for them.
</summary>
</doc>

DockingPortState.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The state of a docking port. See <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DockingPort.State" />.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Ready
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking port is ready to dock to another docking port.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Docked
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking port is docked to another docking port, or docked to
another part (from the VAB/SPH).
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Docking
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking port is very close to another docking port,
but has not docked. It is using magnetic force to acquire a solid dock.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Undocking
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking port has just been undocked from another docking port,
and is disabled until it moves away by a sufficient distance
(<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.DockingPort.ReengageDistance" />).
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Shielded
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking port has a shield, and the shield is closed.
</summary>
</doc>

values.name: Moving
values.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The docking ports shield is currently opening/closing.
</summary>
</doc>

<doc>

The parachute is unsafe to deploy, and will break off.
</summary>
</doc>

<doc>
<summary>
The safety state is not available, because the vessel is not in an

ActionGroupAction.documentation:

<summary>
An action, belonging to a part module, that is assigned to an action group.
Obtained by calling <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Control.GetActionGroupActions" />.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Part
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part that the action acts on.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Module
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module that the action belongs to. Returns <c>null</c> for a
part-level action that is not associated with a module. This only occurs when
the Extended Action Groups mod is installed, as it can assign actions defined
directly on a part, rather than on one of its modules, to an action group.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Name
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The human-readable name of the action, as shown in the action group editor.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Id
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The non-localized identifier for the action.
</summary>
</doc>

RoboticAxis.documentation:

<remarks>

</doc>

fields.name: Module
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The part module the axis belongs to.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: FieldName
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The name of the field the axis controls.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: DataAmount
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Data amount.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: ScienceValue
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Science value.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: TransmitValue
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Transmit value.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Id
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The identifier of the subject, e.g. <c>crewReport@KerbinSrfLandedLaunchPad</c>.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Title
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
The title of the subject, as shown in the science archives.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: IsComplete
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Whether the subject has been fully researched. This is true once the science banked for
the subject reaches the science cap. As the banked science (see <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ScienceSubject.Science" />) is
only updated after transmission/recovery, this reflects fully mining the subject over
repeated experiments, not whether a single run has produced data. To check whether a run
has produced data, and how valuable it is, use <see cref="M:SpaceCenter.Experiment.HasData" /> and
<see cref="M:SpaceCenter.ScienceData.TransmitValue" />.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: Science
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Amount of science already earned from this subject, not updated until after
transmission/recovery.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: ScienceCap
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Total science allowable for this subject.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: DataScale
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Multiply science value by this to determine data amount in mits.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: SubjectValue
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Multiplier for specific Celestial Body/Experiment Situation combination.
</summary>
</doc>

fields.name: ScientificValue
fields.documentation:
<doc>
<summary>
Diminishing value multiplier for decreasing the science value returned from repeated
experiments.
</summary>
</doc>
